rejected_alternative.content: The authors reject the naive substitution of a spatially varying twist angle because distant disorder would unrealistically produce larger displacements.
rejected_alternative.evidence_span: Naively, one would think to promote θ →θ(r) ≡θ0+δθ(r). But there is a problem with this prescription: disorder at points far away from the origin result in larger displacements. This is inconsistent with the observed phenomenology of twisted compounds, where mesoscopic patches of the material are at a consistent uniform twist angle [6].

inspiration_source.content: The modeling approach is motivated by an analogy between twist angle/displacement and magnetic field/vector potential in electrodynamics.
inspiration_source.evidence_span: In analogy to electrodynamics, where the magnetic field is given by the curl of the vector potential, we model the twist angle as the curl of the relative displacement between the two bilayers.

inspiration_source.content: The treatment is guided by an analogy between displacement/twist-angle fields and vector-potential/magnetic-field relations.
inspiration_source.evidence_span: the relation between the displace- ment field and twist angle is exactly analogous to that between the vector potential and magnetic field.

inspiration_source.content: The model is shaped by analogy to charged particles in a static magnetic field, since both map to a nonlinear sigma model after replication.
inspiration_source.evidence_span: Our model is closely related to that of charged particles in a static magnetic field; in both cases, the replicated action can be mapped onto a NLSM.

inspiration_source.content: The treatment is guided by the static magnetic field case from Ref. [5].
inspiration_source.evidence_span: Relative to the case of a static magnetic field studied in Ref. [5], the symmetry is reduced; here, different harmonics with the same m quantum number can mix.

causal_claim.content: Local twist-geometry changes cause spatially correlated changes in the Hamiltonian and thereby affect transport and ordering.
causal_claim.evidence_span: a local change in the twist geometry can give rise to spatially-correlated alterations of the parent Hamiltonian, which in turn affect the coarse-grained properties of the substrate such as transport and ordering tendencies.

causal_claim.content: Twist structure imposes geometric scattering constraints that suppress momentum relaxation compared with white noise.
causal_claim.evidence_span: We find that geometric scattering constraints imposed here by the twist structure substantially suppress momentum relaxation relative to mean-rate-matched white noise.

causal_claim.content: Tweaking the kernel power spectrum sharpens the gradient
causal_claim.evidence_span: We can tweak the power spectrum of the kernel to sharpen the gradient.

causal_claim.content: The first-order disorder contribution only renormalizes the moiré potential to one set by the mean twist angle.
causal_claim.evidence_span: It is straightforward to see that the first-order effect, S(1) dis, entails nothing more than putting fermions in a effective moir´e potential defined by the mean twist angle.

causal_claim.content: Disorder averaging introduces a correlation between fermion density operators.
causal_claim.evidence_span: As in the conventional impurity scattering case, the dis- order average introduces a correlation g(r, r′) between fermion density operators.

causal_claim.content: The oscillating sign of the correlation causes both positive and negative effective inter-replica correlations.
causal_claim.evidence_span: First of all, notice that the sign of g(r, r′) oscillates in space. This means that both positive and negative effective correlations will be induced between replicas.

causal_claim.content: Near k ≃ qμ, the scattering processes become strongly singular.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Indeed, processes for which k ≃qµ are strongly singular [56].

causal_claim.content: Because the Fermi wave-vector is set by filling, disorder effects should depend strongly on filling.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The Fermi wave-vector kF is deter- mined by filling factor. Therefore, one expects that the effects of disorder can depend strongly on filling.

causal_claim.content: The microscopic Hamiltonian's time-reversal symmetry determines the Altland-Zirnbauer universality class of the long-distance theory.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Depending on the time- reversal symmetry of the microscopic Hamiltonian, the long-distance theory can be identified with one of several Altland-Zirnbauer universality classes.

causal_claim.content: Larger diffusivity indicates twist-angle disorder relaxes momentum less effectively than Anderson disorder.
causal_claim.evidence_span: This indicates that the twist-angle disorder is less effective at relaxing momentum, due to the added structure of the disorder-replicated kernel.

causal_claim.content: The results suggest the twist disorder kernel is much less effective at relaxing momentum.
causal_claim.evidence_span: This suggests that the twist disorder kernel is substantially less effective at re- laxing momentum

causal_claim.content: Weaker localization from twist-angle disorder has important consequences for the stability of correlated phases across moiré platforms.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The fact that twist-angle disorder is less strongly localising than its Anderson counterpart has im- portant consequences for understanding the stability of correlated phases, e.g., superconductivity and fractional quantum Hall, across moir´e platforms.

causal_claim.content: Because the quantities converge as the regularizer vanishes, the singularity is concluded not to obscure the physics.
causal_claim.evidence_span: As a result, we conclude that the singularity is not obscuring the relevant physics.

causal_claim.content: Because the disorder correlation length exceeds the moiré lattice scale, one can average over the center-of-mass coordinate over a moiré unit cell.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Because the correlation length of the disorder is much larger than the moire lattice scale, we can average over the centre-of-mass coordinate Rcm over a single moire unit cell.

causal_claim.content: The small-k velocity-coupling term causes diffusion by coupling density and massive angular modes.
causal_claim.evidence_span: At small k, the term proportional to k · vF couples the density mode to the massive angular modes; this is how diffusion arises.

causal_claim.content: The diffusion constant is obtained from the quadratic small-k dispersion.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The diffusion constant can be extracting by fitting the small-k behaviour to a quadratic dispersion.

mechanism_principle.content: The enhanced diffusivity/localization-length increase is attributed to the intricate scattering kernel structure inherited from deviations from rigid twist, which spreads correlations over large scales.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: We believe this to be, in part, attributable to the intricate structure of the scattering kernel—inherited from the fact that we are considering deviations from a rigid twist, which can dispatch correlations across large scales.

mechanism_principle.content: The filling dependence arises because singular scattering on the Fermi surface occurs when 2kF is close to q0.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: If we assume that scattering is taking place on the Fermi surface, this corresponds to the condition that 2kF ≃q0, where q0 ≡|qµ|. The Fermi wave-vector kF is deter- mined by filling factor. Therefore, one expects that the effects of disorder can depend strongly on filling.

mechanism_principle.content: The reduced momentum relaxation is attributed to added structure in the disorder-replicated kernel.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: due to the added structure of the disorder-replicated kernel

mechanism_principle.content: This reduced momentum relaxation is partly due to the kernel's intricate geometric structure.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: owed in part to its intricate geomet- ric structure.

mechanism_principle.content: The sign of the induced correlation oscillates spatially, implying both positive and negative effective inter-replica correlations.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: First of all, notice that the sign of g(r, r′) oscillates in space. This means that both positive and negative effective correlations will be induced between replicas.

mechanism_principle.content: Diffusion emerges because the small-k velocity term couples the density mode to massive angular modes.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: At small k, the term proportional to k · vF couples the density mode to the massive angular modes; this is how diffusion arises.

hypothesis_statement.content: For small twist-angle disorder, the clean-limit moiré potential form remains valid and disorder enters only through the displacement fields
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: In the presence of angle disorder this translation invariance is broken, but for small twist-angle disorder we make the approximation that the form ∆(r) remains valid; disor- der effects enter only through uℓ(r).

hypothesis_statement.content: The essential effects of disorder are proposed to reside in the second-order term rather than the first-order one.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: Thus the essential disorder physics is actually encoded in the second-order term

hypothesis_statement.content: The work assumes trigonal warping of the Fermi surface.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: If we assume a trigonally-warped Fermi surface, then dµ(ϕ) ≃dϕ 2π (1 + δ cos 3ϕ)

hypothesis_statement.content: The work assumes velocity anisotropy does not strongly affect the geometric arc-length factor.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: We assume that the velocity anisotropy does not significantly modify the geometric arc-length factor.

evidence_result.content: The study finds strong suppression of momentum relaxation from twist-structure-induced scattering constraints.
evidence_result.evidence_span: We find that geometric scattering constraints imposed here by the twist structure substantially suppress momentum relaxation relative to mean-rate-matched white noise.

evidence_result.content: The problem is shown to map onto a non-linear sigma model.
evidence_result.evidence_span: We quantify these effects and show that the problem can be mapped onto a non-linear sigma model (NLSM).

evidence_result.content: Power-law and Lorentz-correlated disorder produce domain walls, but they are not sharply resolved
evidence_result.evidence_span: Plotting θ(r) and |∇θ(r)| for these three disorder config- urations in Fig. 1, we see that domain walls begin to ap- pear for the power-law and Lorentz-correlated disorder. However, the domain walls—a key experimental observa- tion [6]—are poorly resolved.

evidence_result.content: Using the extended power spectrum yields a spatial twist-angle distribution matching experiment
evidence_result.evidence_span: The twist angle in space, as well as its gradient, is plotted in the rightmost panel of Fig. 1 for α = 2. The spatial distribution of θ(r) now matches that of experiment, see Ref. [6].

evidence_result.content: For white-noise disorder, the averaged coupling has a form closely resembling that of static random magnetic field problems.
evidence_result.evidence_span: When S(k) = 1 (white noise), the functional form of ¯g(k) is strongly reminiscent of what one finds in the presence of a static random magnetic field [5].

evidence_result.content: The low-energy theory is reformulated as a nonlinear sigma model via a retarded-advanced generating functional.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Non-linear sigma model. The generating functional for a two-particle Green’s function of the retarded- advanced type may be represented as a functional in- tegral over a field ψ

evidence_result.content: Numerical results confirm the diffuson sector has the expected long-wavelength form with one conserved density mode and other angular modes massive.
evidence_result.evidence_span: We confirm numerically in Fig. 2 that the diffuson sector has the expected long-wavelength form Γ(k, ω) ∼−iω + Dijkikj + . . . , with one conserved density mode and all other angular modes massive.

evidence_result.content: For the trigonal-warping numerics, the nonlinear sigma model falls in class A.
evidence_result.evidence_span: For the trigonal warping case presented in the numerics, the NLSM is in class A.

evidence_result.content: Across all kernels, twist-angle disorder yields larger diffusivity than the matched Anderson reference.
evidence_result.evidence_span: We see that in all cases the diffusivity associated with twist-angle disorder is larger than that of the Anderson reference.

evidence_result.content: The extended angle-disorder correlation kernel shows the strongest diffusivity enhancement.
evidence_result.evidence_span: In fact, the enhanced diffusivity is strongest in the ‘extended’ angle disorder correlation kernel, which offers the closest match to experiment [6].

evidence_result.content: Numerics show diffusivity is several orders of magnitude larger than for mean-rate-matched white noise.
evidence_result.evidence_span: We show numer- 5 ically that the resulting diffusivity is larger—by several orders of magnitude—than that which would result from mean-rate-matched white noise.

evidence_result.content: Calculated physical quantities converge as the regularizer goes to zero.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The physical quan- tities we later calculate, e.g., the diffusivity, converge as the regularizer is taken to zero.

evidence_result.content: The numerical calculation stays well controlled as the regularizer goes to zero.
evidence_result.evidence_span: We find that the numerics remain well-controlled even as κIR →0, see Fig. S1.

evidence_result.content: Figure S1 shows isotropic diffusivity converges as the regularizer is reduced to zero.
evidence_result.evidence_span: FIG. S1. Isotropic diffusivity calculated for the four covariance kernels described earlier, sweeping the small regularizer κIR. We find that the calculation converges as we take κIR →0.

evidence_result.content: Figure S1 shows isotropic diffusivity converges as the IR regularizer is taken to zero.
evidence_result.evidence_span: FIG. S1. Isotropic diffusivity calculated for the four covariance kernels described earlier, sweeping the small regularizer κIR. We find that the calculation converges as we take κIR →0.

constraint.content: The disorder model must remain consistent with observed mesoscopic patches having a uniform twist angle.
constraint.evidence_span: This is inconsistent with the observed phenomenology of twisted compounds, where mesoscopic patches of the material are at a consistent uniform twist angle [6].

constraint.content: The analysis is restricted to weak twist-angle disorder so perturbation theory applies.

constraint.content: The Wigner-transform and moiré-cell averaging step assumes disorder correlations are much longer ranged than the moiré lattice scale.

constraint.content: Soft modes are identified only in the small-momentum and small-frequency limit.

evidence_spans: If we assume that scattering is taking place on the Fermi surface, this corresponds to the condition that 2kF ≃q0, where q0 ≡|qµ|. The Fermi wave-vector kF is deter- mined by filling factor. Therefore, one expects that the effects of disorder can depend strongly on filling.

mechanism_principle.content: The induced correlation oscillates in sign across space, implying both positive and negative effective inter-replica correlations.
evidence_spans: First of all, notice that the sign of g(r, r′) oscillates in space. This means that both positive and negative effective correlations will be induced between replicas.

mechanism_principle.content: Diffusion arises because, at small k, the k·vF velocity term couples the density mode to massive angular modes.
evidence_spans: At small k, the term proportional to k · vF couples the density mode to the massive angular modes; this is how diffusion arises.

hypothesis_statement.content: For small twist-angle disorder, the clean-limit moiré potential form remains valid, with disorder entering through the displacement fields; under this treatment, the essential effects of disorder are proposed to be encoded primarily in the second-order term rather than the first-order one.
evidence_spans: In the presence of angle disorder this translation invariance is broken, but for small twist-angle disorder we make the approximation that the form ∆(r) remains valid; disor- der effects enter only through uℓ(r).
Thus the essential disorder physics is actually encoded in the second-order term

hypothesis_statement.content: The analysis assumes a trigonally warped Fermi surface.
evidence_spans: If we assume a trigonally-warped Fermi surface, then dµ(ϕ) ≃dϕ 2π (1 + δ cos 3ϕ)

hypothesis_statement.content: The analysis assumes that velocity anisotropy does not significantly modify the geometric arc-length factor.
evidence_spans: We assume that the velocity anisotropy does not significantly modify the geometric arc-length factor.

evidence_result.content: Twist-structure-induced geometric scattering constraints strongly suppress momentum relaxation and lead to diffusivity much larger—by several orders of magnitude than mean-rate-matched white-noise/Anderson reference disorder; across all kernels, twist-angle disorder has larger diffusivity, with the extended angle-disorder correlation kernel showing the strongest enhancement.
evidence_spans: We find that geometric scattering constraints imposed here by the twist structure substantially suppress momentum relaxation relative to mean-rate-matched white noise.
We see that in all cases the diffusivity associated with twist-angle disorder is larger than that of the Anderson reference.
In fact, the enhanced diffusivity is strongest in the ‘extended’ angle disorder correlation kernel, which offers the closest match to experiment [6].
We show numer- 5 ically that the resulting diffusivity is larger—by several orders of magnitude—than that which would result from mean-rate-matched white noise.

evidence_result.content: The disorder problem / low-energy theory can be reformulated as a nonlinear sigma model using a retarded-advanced generating functional; for the trigonal-warping numerics, the resulting NLSM is in class A.
evidence_spans: We quantify these effects and show that the problem can be mapped onto a non-linear sigma model (NLSM).

evidence_result.content: Numerics confirm the diffuson sector has the expected long-wavelength form, with one conserved density mode and all other angular modes massive.
evidence_spans: We confirm numerically in Fig. 2 that the diffuson sector has the expected long-wavelength form Γ(k, ω) ∼−iω + Dijkikj + . . . , with one conserved density mode and all other angular modes massive.

evidence_result.content: Simple power-law and Lorentz-correlated disorder produce emerging but poorly resolved domain walls, whereas using the extended power spectrum yields a spatial twist-angle distribution that matches experiment.
evidence_spans: Plotting θ(r) and |∇θ(r)| for these three disorder config- urations in Fig. 1, we see that domain walls begin to ap- pear for the power-law and Lorentz-correlated disorder. However, the domain walls—a key experimental observa- tion [6]—are poorly resolved.
The twist angle in space, as well as its gradient, is plotted in the rightmost panel of Fig. 1 for α = 2. The spatial distribution of θ(r) now matches that of experiment, see Ref. [6].

evidence_result.content: For white-noise disorder, the averaged coupling takes a form strongly reminiscent of static random magnetic field problems.
evidence_spans: When S(k) = 1 (white noise), the functional form of ¯g(k) is strongly reminiscent of what one finds in the presence of a static random magnetic field [5].
